Likelihood ratio tests for drmTMB models

Source: R/anova.R
anova.drmTMB.Rd

Compares two or more models fitted to the same data by likelihood ratio tests, e.g. a model with and without covariates in fform, with and without random effects, or a poisson and a negative binomial model. A model with model="constant" as the smaller model tests for a dose effect.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'drmTMB'
anova(
  object,
  ...,
  test = c("Chisq", "F", "boot"),
  nsim = 1000,
  seed = NULL,
  progress = interactive()
)

Arguments

object

a drmTMB object

...

further drmTMB objects

test

"Chisq" (default) for likelihood ratio tests, "F" for F-tests of gaussian or lognormal models without random effects, priors, correlation structure and variance function, or "boot" for parametric bootstrap likelihood ratio tests

nsim

number of simulations for test="boot"

seed

an optional seed for the random number generator, for test="boot"

progress

logical, show a progress bar for test="boot"

Value

a data frame of class anova with the number of parameters (npar), AIC, BIC, log-likelihood and deviance (minus twice the log-likelihood) of each model, and the likelihood ratio statistic (Chisq), its degrees of freedom (Df) and p-value (Pr(>Chisq)) for the comparison with the previous model. For test="F", the residual degrees of freedom (Res.Df) and residual sum of squares (RSS) instead of the deviance, and the F statistic (F) and its p-value (Pr(>F)). For test="boot", additionally the bootstrap p-value (Pr(boot)), with the simulated likelihood ratio statistics of each comparison in the attribute "boot".

Details

The models are ordered by their number of parameters, and each model is compared with the previous one: the likelihood ratio statistic is twice the difference of their log-likelihoods (the Laplace approximation of the marginal log-likelihoods for models with random effects), with the difference in the number of parameters as degrees of freedom. The test assumes that the smaller model is nested in the larger one, which is not checked. For parameters on the boundary of their range under the smaller model, e.g. a standard deviation of random effects of zero, or an infinite size of the negative binomial for the poisson model, the chi-square distribution is conservative: the p-value is approximately twice the correct value for a single standard deviation.

For gaussian and lognormal (on the log scale) models without random effects, priors, correlation structure and variance function, test="F" gives F-tests, as drc does for continuous responses: the reduction of the (weighted) residual sum of squares per additional parameter, divided by the residual mean square of the largest model, with n - p residual degrees of freedom for p coefficients b1-b5. The F-test is exact for linear models and accounts for the estimation of the residual variance, which the likelihood ratio test does not, so it is usually preferable for small experiments.

test="boot" gives parametric bootstrap likelihood ratio tests, as PBmodcomp of the package pbkrtest: for each comparison, nsim responses are simulated from the smaller model, with new random effects, both models are fitted to each of them, and the p-value Pr(boot) is the proportion of the simulated likelihood ratio statistics at least as large as the observed one, (1 + #{LR* >= LR}) / (1 + nsim). It does not rely on the chi-square distribution, which is only approximate in small samples, for parameters on the boundary (standard deviations of random effects of zero, the poisson model within the negative binomial), and for parameters that are not identified under the smaller model (e.g. the steepness and location of the curve compared with model="constant"). The chi-square p-value is shown for comparison. Each model is fitted twice to each simulated response, starting at its estimates and at the starting values of drmTMB, and the better fit is used; simulations without a finite log-likelihood of both models are left out.

References

Halekoh, U. and Hojsgaard, S. (2014). A Kenward-Roger approximation and parametric bootstrap methods for tests in linear mixed models - the R package pbkrtest. Journal of Statistical Software 59(9), 1-32.

See also

drmTMB (model="constant" for a test of a dose effect), bootstrap

Examples

mod <- drmTMB(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = "loglogistic",
              start = c(b1 = 0, b5 = 0), fix = c(b1 = TRUE, b5 = TRUE))
# a free lower asymptote b1
mod4 <- drmTMB(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = "loglogistic",
               start = c(b5 = 0), fix = c(b5 = TRUE))
anova(mod, mod4)
#> Likelihood ratio tests of drmTMB models
#> 
#>      npar    AIC    BIC  logLik deviance Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)  
#> mod     4 45.208 49.920 -18.604   37.208                      
#> mod4    5 42.310 48.201 -16.155   32.310 4.898  1    0.02689 *
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
anova(mod, mod4, test = "F")
#> F-tests of drmTMB models
#> 
#>      npar    AIC    BIC  logLik Res.Df    RSS     F Df  Pr(>F)  
#> mod     4 45.208 49.920 -18.604     21 6.6228                   
#> mod4    5 42.310 48.201 -16.155     20 5.4002 4.528  1 0.04597 *
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
# test for any dose effect, against a constant mean
mod0 <- drmTMB(rootl ~ conc, data = ryegrass, model = "constant")
anova(mod0, mod)
#> Likelihood ratio tests of drmTMB models
#> 
#>      npar     AIC    BIC  logLik deviance Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)    
#> mod0    2 128.188 130.54 -62.094  124.188                        
#> mod     4  45.208  49.92 -18.604   37.208 86.98  2  < 2.2e-16 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
